questions.q: Per this lesson, what is the key difference between an audit and monitoring?
options: An audit answers one question once; monitoring answers many questions on a recurring schedule
An audit only applies to QUERY_HISTORY, monitoring only to ACCESS_HISTORY
Monitoring requires a third-party tool outside Snowflake
An audit is automated, monitoring is always manual
questions.explain: The lesson draws a clear line: audits investigate something that already happened, once; monitoring runs many such checks continuously to catch gaps early.

questions.q: What real Snowflake object does this lesson use to schedule a governance check?
options: A Task, created with CREATE TASK and a SCHEDULE clause
A Stream, created with CREATE STREAM
A Stage, created with CREATE STAGE
A Sequence, created with CREATE SEQUENCE
questions.explain: CREATE TASK with a SCHEDULE clause (a CRON expression or simple interval) is Snowflake's real mechanism for running a SQL statement on a recurring schedule.

questions.q: In the lesson's CREATE TASK example, what does the SCHEDULE clause 'USING CRON 0 7 * * * America/New_York' specify?
options: Run once daily at 7:00 AM Eastern time
Run every 7 minutes
Run once a year on day 7 of month 7
Run continuously with no scheduled interval
questions.explain: The five CRON fields (minute hour day month day-of-week) of '0 7 * * *' mean 7:00 AM every day, in the specified America/New_York timezone.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the four monitoring categories this lesson names?
options: New privileged role grants (e.g. ACCOUNTADMIN)
Spikes in failed logins
Sensitive columns with no masking policy applied
The visual theme of the Snowsight UI
questions.explain: The four real categories are privileged grants, failed-login spikes, policy coverage gaps, and warehouse spend anomalies — UI theming isn't a governance signal.

questions.q: Why does a Task need a WAREHOUSE specified in its definition?
options: A Task runs a SQL statement like any other query, and needs a warehouse to supply the compute to execute it
WAREHOUSE is only required for tasks that write to external stages
It determines which role owns the task
It sets the task's retry policy
questions.explain: A Task executes real SQL on a schedule, and like any query, that execution needs compute — supplied by the named virtual warehouse.
